record.context_brief: Existence of Steiner solutions for non-closed bounded inputs
record.original_question: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be a bounded set (not assumed closed). Consider the optimization problem: find a set S such that H^1(S) is minimal among all sets with S \cup A connected. Is it possible that this problem has no solution for some bounded A \subset \mathbb{R}^d, i.e., that the infimum of H^1(S) over admissible S is not attained? (Equivalently, is the closedness assumption on A necessary for solvability in this formulation?)

evidence.quote:
Question 2.3. Is it possible to find a bounded set A ⊂ Rd such that the problem: “find S such that H1 (S) is minimal
among all sets for which S ∪ A is connected” does not have a solution?
   This question was asked by E. Paolini, who is interested whether the assumption that A ⊂ Rd is closed is necessary for
the problem to be solvable.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $d \geq 2$ and let $\mathcal{H}^1$ denote the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Given a bounded set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (not assumed to be closed), consider the variational problem of minimizing $\mathcal{H}^1(S)$ among all sets $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $S \cup A$ is connected. Determine whether there exists a bounded set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ for which this minimization problem admits no solution; that is, for which the infimum $\inf\{\mathcal{H}^1(S) : S \cup A \text{ is connected}\}$ is not attained. Equivalently, decide whether the hypothesis that $A$ be closed is necessary for the existence of a minimizer.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is attributed to E. Paolini and appears as an open problem. Existence results for the Steiner problem are typically established under the assumption that the input set is closed/compact (so that its closure is compact and standard existence arguments apply). No source located in the search resolves whether a bounded non-closed input can produce a non-attained infimum, so the status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and regularity results for the Steiner problem
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theorems for the Steiner problem are formulated for compact input sets C in a complete metric space.
status_evidence.claim: Standard existence results assume the input set is compact/closed, leaving the bounded non-closed case unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Minimal connections: the classical Steiner problem and generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Steiner problem and its generalizations by Paolini and collaborators.
status_evidence.claim: Paolini's work poses existence questions for the Steiner problem; the non-closed bounded case is raised as a question.
